pl-l4d3c7-d1e115.summary: Answers how immersion should be done: once or three times, according to the varying custom of the Church.
claims: Immersion may be single or triple.

pl-l4d3c7-d1e118.summary: Quotes Gregory: in one faith differing custom does no harm to the Church. Since there is one substance in three subsistences, it is not blameworthy to immerse an infant three times or once, for the three immersions can signify the Trinity of persons and one the singleness of the divinity; those who immerse three times also signify the sacrament of the three days' burial.
claims: Diverse custom does not harm unity of faith.
Triple immersion signifies the persons and the burial; single, the one divinity.

pl-l4d3c7-d1e127.summary: Draws out that, accordingly, it is lawful to immerse not only three times but also once.

pl-l4d3c7-d1e131.summary: Restricts this: single immersion is lawful only where it is the Church's custom; one who begins it where it is not the custom, or asserts that only one immersion should be made, makes himself blameworthy.
claims: Single immersion is lawful only where customary.
Asserting that only single immersion is right is blameworthy.

pl-l4d3c7-d1e134.summary: Quotes Haymo: Cyprian abounded in his own sense when he immersed infants once, zealously doing what he understood and abounding in good works, though unknowingly at fault; because of his good works, God later corrected him and he immersed them three times.
claims: Cyprian erred in immersing once and was later corrected.

pl-l4d3c7-d1e140.summary: Draws out that the one who immersed once sinned, but because his church's custom was otherwise or because he asserted that only one immersion should be made.
claims: Single immersion is faulty against custom or when asserted as exclusive.

pl-l4d3c7-d1e143.summary: Quotes Augustine on triple immersion: after promising to believe, we were immersed three times; rightly, having received baptism in the name of the Trinity, and rightly, in the name of Christ who rose on the third day, since the threefold immersion expresses the type of the Lord's burial.
claims: Triple immersion signifies the Trinity and Christ's three days in the tomb.

pl-l4d3c7-d1e152.summary: Concludes that those to be baptized ought to be immersed three times, yet if immersed once they receive true baptism; one who immerses once does not sin unless the Church's custom forbids it or he asserts that it must be done only so.
claims: Triple immersion is the norm, but single immersion is valid.
Single immersion is sinful only against custom or when made exclusive.

pl-l4d3c7.summary: Holds that immersion may be single or triple, according to the varying custom of the Church. Gregory: in one faith differing custom does no harm; triple immersion signifies the three persons, single the one divinity, and triple also the three days' burial. One may immerse once only where that is the custom; whoever introduces it elsewhere or asserts it alone is right is blameworthy, as Haymo says Cyprian was before God corrected him. Augustine explains triple immersion as signifying the Trinity and the three days' burial. So the baptized ought to be immersed three times, yet a single immersion gives true baptism and is not a sin unless against custom or asserted as the only way.
claims: Immersion may be single or triple, by custom of the Church.
Triple immersion signifies the Trinity and the three days' burial; single signifies the one divinity.
Single immersion against custom, or insisting on it alone, is blameworthy.
A single immersion still gives true baptism.
